races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Dee's Mochafella
runners_data.note: Running style unknown with lightly raced profile — trainer Fionn McSharry records 0/3 over 14 days and there is no form string to read, so tactical placement and true ability are genuinely opaque going into this race.

runners_data.name: Mad Jack
runners_data.note: Another unknown quantity for Ed de Giles, whose 14-day strike rate of 0/6 offers little encouragement; with no form to assess and style unclassified, this runner adds uncertainty but is difficult to construct a positive case around without evidence.

runners_data.name: Old Oak
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who finished last on debut over 6f on good ground, and carries a fade-in-finish flag — the step up to a mile is logical but Richard Hannon's yard has been active (4/55) and the 37-day absence adds mild doubt; will need a truly searching gallop that this race is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with two outings on good ground showing placed form (7th, 3rd) — Tim Easterby's yard is very busy (4/73) and David Allan takes the ride, but being a genuine hold-up type in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to set him up is a tactical concern over this mile trip.

runners_data.name: Scarlet Dynasty
runners_data.note: Drops back from 7f with two eighth-place finishes on good ground and a fade-in-finish flag — Gemma Tutty's small yard (2/17) and Kaiya Fraser in the saddle are modest components, and nothing in the profile suggests a reversal of recent form here.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.note: Prominent-running type who ran 2nd over 7f on good ground last time out for Adrian Keatley — M. P. Sheehy rides and the step to a mile should suit a horse who travels handy and finishes; handily placed for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Coral Cove
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground and followed up with a second — James Owen's yard is in good nick (7/45) and Jason Hart is an astute partner; prominent style is ideally suited to an uncontested tempo in front of a large field and this is the most course-ready profile in the race.

runners_data.name: Bedwyr
runners_data.note: Prominent type who has shown modest form (5th, 10th) on good and standard surfaces — Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood send him here 27 days after his last run; better form needed but style is at least aligned with the race shape.

runners_data.name: Nosey Book
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 3rd and 6th on good ground for Tim Easterby, and notable for wearing headgear (hg:p) — Duran Fentiman rides and the 15-day turnaround suggests the yard is happy; front-end positioning suits and the hood could aid concentration over the mile.

runners_data.name: Special Operations
runners_data.note: Unknown-style runner by classification but holds one run (4th on good ground for Tim Easterby) — Sean Kirrane takes the ride and the going is not a concern, but with minimal evidence the ability level is hard to pin down; Easterby's yard volume is significant context.

runners_data.name: Temple Court
runners_data.note: Holds genuine hold-up form across four starts (including a 3rd over 7f on good ground for Eve Johnson Houghton) — with the field packed with hold-up types, Temple Court is likely to be shuffled further forward than ideal, meaning Callum Hutchinson will be riding a different race from the horse's natural pattern; its chance should be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: London Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who finished 8th on soft/standard ground over 7f — 51 days off the track is the longest absence in the field, Ollie Pears records 0/10 in 14 days, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the structural difficulty of this race shape; few positives to anchor.

runners_data.name: Tommo's Queen
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and likely to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop — Joanna Mason rides for Michael & David Easterby (3/29 in 14 days) and the mare's one run shows a 4th on good ground over 7f; the style-fit tag reflects she may find herself pressed further in front than is comfortable, but with no rival to challenge her for the lead she should control the fractions.

races.paceDynamic: Tommo's Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, should dictate from the outset at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Ripon's flat mile. With 13 runners but only one horse naturally wired to lead, the pace is unlikely to be searingly strong, meaning the early tempo is set by Tommo's Queen alone and the field will string out behind her at a rhythm she chooses. The prominent types — Coral Cove, The First Drop, Nosey Book, and Bedwyr — will compete for the positions immediately behind the leader, which is where the race will be won and lost. This race shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can travel handy, avoid traffic trouble in a 13-runner field, and produce a sustained finish rather than a late sprint off a slow pace; genuine hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage because the pace is not fast enough to set them up. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can place cleanly at the rear — Temple Court is a genuine hold-up horse that will likely find itself further forward than ideal, meaning its natural finishing style may be compromised.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Tommo's Queen sets an uncontested, even gallop and the race is decided by those who travel handy throughout.
scenarios.body: Tommo's Queen dictates on her own terms, and the prominent runners immediately behind her — Coral Cove, The First Drop, and Nosey Book — track her through the race and use their position to strike as the field straightens for home. True hold-up horses are left with too little ground to make up and a pace that never genuinely stretched the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is just brisk enough to briefly expose Tommo's Queen and one or two prominent runners fade, creating a gap for a well-positioned midfielders to come through.
scenarios.body: Rule Of The Agency or Special Operations, tracking in mid-division without being committed too early, finds a clear run in the straight and picks off tiring leaders in the final furlong. This only materialises if the early pace has more zip than expected given the competitive prominent group vying for position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Tommo's Queen and the fastest-reacting prominent horse steal an uncontested break that the hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: A slow, dawdling pace in a large field creates a scenario where two or three up front simply gallop away from rivals who have never been able to get competitive, with the hold-up brigade stuck in traffic with no cover.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners over-race in their battle for positions and bleed their finishing effort, leaving a rare opening for genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Old Oak or London Rose, genuinely held up at the rear, might benefit if a contested pace between prominent rivals burns them out in the final quarter-mile; however, both carry fading-finish flags and Temple Court is racing out of its true hold-up role, making this the least structurally supported shape.

watchPoints.text: Coral Cove has the clearest form profile (a win and a second on good ground) and a prominent style that maps perfectly to this race shape — watch for Jason Hart to slot in directly behind Tommo's Queen and never leave the front two.

Nosey Book wears headgear (hood) for Tim Easterby — if the headgear improves focus and concentration over the mile trip, the market may underestimate a horse who tracks the pace from a handy position and improves on previous form figures.

Temple Court is a genuine hold-up type that will be racing out of its natural role in a field where hold-up positions are over-subscribed — watch to see whether Callum Hutchinson can find any daylight from an unfamiliar position, or whether the horse is simply compromised throughout.

With 13 runners in a novice field on a flat mile circuit, early traffic and jostling for prominent positions is a real risk — watch the start closely, as The First Drop and Bedwyr may tangle for position behind Tommo's Queen in the first furlong.

Tommo's Queen's gallop tempo is the controlling variable for the entire race — if Joanna Mason allows an unusually slow pace, the hold-up horses will be left hopelessly stranded and the race becomes a sprint finish from the front; monitor the early splits closely.

races.name: Racing For Tamara Ripon Hornblower EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
William Hill Supporting MND Silver Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Ruth Carr in strong form (2nd twice lately), handles good ground comfortably across 13 of 15 outings, but no wins in five similar-going starts — needs to secure a clean berth early in this congested field or risks being shuffled back in the scrimmage; visor worn.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Woodstock at least shows consistency with two seconds in recent outings, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 134 lb from stall ten, his rating of 80 offers some encouragement, though a first win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Roberto Caro
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Adrian Keatley whose recent form reads bleakly (three zeros), has only one win on similar going from six tries, and 5f/6f turf form on good shows heavy traffic vulnerability; needs something to go wrong for others.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Roberto Caro has been unplaced in his three most recent outings, though a third four starts back shows he retains some ability; experience over today's trip and going helps, but 134 lb from stall 18 makes things harder.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for Nigel Tinkler with two wins on good ground from 11 attempts — has the profile to slot in just behind Kats Bob if he avoids the early bunching, and his 1-2-4-2-1 recent form string is the standout record in the field.
runners_data.comment: Magic Boy won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but a seventh last time out tempers enthusiasm, and carrying 134 lb from stall 14 adds to the challenge for this mid-division type.

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Tim Easterby, handles good ground well (12 from 15) but has struggled to convert strong position into wins in this type, and at 3yo carrying 132lbs she faces a stiff task from the back against older rivals who know this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Anaisa nonetheless brings distance and going experience into this, and a rating of 84 suggests she holds strong claims on form — the worry is a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for David Allan/Easterby, consistent on good ground (9 from 15) but tends to peak at 5f — this 6f test on a big field day risks finding him outpaced at the death having used energy in the early prominent battle.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a fourth two starts back, Go Vince Go arrives on a handy 22-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going; winless in his last six starts, but our ratings just about place him top of this 20-runner field despite a trainer out of form.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Prominent type for David Nolan and Paul Midgley with a solid 6f good-ground profile (11 from 15, two wins), a fresh-ish 10-day gap, and the talent to lock in a clean position if he jumps well; no headgear flag and trainer quiet recently, but one of the more credible placed threats.
runners_data.comment: Emperor Caradoc has been winless in his last six starts, with a pair of fourths in his most recent outings doing little to inspire confidence, and ranked fifteenth of twenty on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and ten days since his last run leaves him fit enough.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse back after just 9 days, has won twice on similar going and loves 6f; his last run was a win at standard and he has place form on good ground, making him a lively each-way candidate if he finds clear passage from deep.
runners_data.comment: Dorney Lake has shown he can win at this level, with a victory last time out and a second three starts back, but ranked 18 of 20 on our figures he faces a stiff task, and 131 lb from stall 20 adds further complication; experience over today's trip and going is the one genuine plus.

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Oliver Stammers, carries a chunky 138lbs and has failed to win in five outings on good ground in this dataset — an R (refused) in recent form adds a fitness/temperament question, making him harder to trust at the top of the weights.
runners_data.comment: Westmorian has run over today's trip and going before, and his 28-day break looks well-timed for this return, with our rating of 84 marking him out as a leading contender among 20 rivals; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Roach Power
runners_data.note: Prominent in theory but often races at 5f and has produced declining form at 6f on good ground (two 19th-place finishes in last five), returning after a 68-day break; long absence and step back up in trip make this a watch-and-see run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and not seen out for 68 days, Roach Power does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, but stall 16 and a 137 lb burden make life no easier for a horse who has to find significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Joanna Mason and Roger Fell with a spectacular recent record — three consecutive wins on good ground (1-1-1 in last three similar-going starts from ten tries total) — the most in-form horse in the race if she can thread through late.
runners_data.comment: Glory Hyde won three of her last six starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, but has disappointed in her last two outings; she has run over today's trip and going, yet carries 136 lb from stall 19 and an official mark of 78 leaves her with little in hand.

runners_data.name: Mythical Composer
runners_data.note: Prominent type for Clive Cox who has never won on good ground in five tries (0W2P) and whose most recent run was a 23rd of 23 on similar going — pace headgear and recent trainer form of 3/18 offer marginal optimism but the form line is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has been unplaced most recently, and that inconsistency is the concern here; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 136 lb from stall 15, there is plenty to overcome if he is to recapture that winning form.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed leader for William Pyle and Ruth Carr, wearing a visor, with five placed efforts on good ground and a recent consistent string (2-2-7-20-4) — likely to control early fractions unchallenged but has not won in current form cycle.
runners_data.comment: Kats Bob has finished second in each of his last two starts and arrives here fresh on 17 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts and a midfield ranking on ratings suggest he'll need to find a touch more to go one better.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Jason Hart flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with three recent finishes in double figures on good ground — Midgley trainer draw is cold (0/19 in 14 days) and the late-fade tendency makes him very hard to back here.
runners_data.comment: Grant Wood has run over today's trip and going, and his fourth last time out hints at a return to form — ranked third of 20 on our figures, he carries 135 lb from stall seven and represents a genuine threat, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose inclination to race up with the pace is credibly real, but with eight prominent-types ahead of him in the pecking order he is likely to be displaced into midfield in practice; his 12-from-15 good-ground record is solid and he has recent place form, though racing out of his preferred position dulls the chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Mister Sox is winless in his last six starts, though a second and a third in recent outings show he retains some ability; he has run over today's distance and going before, arrives on a quick turnaround of ten days, but connections saddle him from a trainer operating at just five per cent recently, which is a concern.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, assigned to midfield on the map because the rear is over-subscribed — he fades in the finish flag, seven-year-old with mediocre recent figures at this trip, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 suggests his chance is compressed by not finding his natural racing berth.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tolstoy has experience of today's trip and conditions but his two most recent runs ended in unplaced efforts, and carrying 130 lb from stall 12 offers no easy route back into contention.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Andrew Mullen with two recent wins at 5f and 7f, but only two from eight tries on good ground at 6f specifically — his natural position in the prominent group is genuine and he has live winning form, making him a credible if underrated player if he gets a clean pitch.
runners_data.comment: She ran unplaced last time out after back-to-back wins two and three starts back, and ranked 19 of 20 on our figures she faces a stiff ask here, though experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after 22 days, offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Duran Fentiman, back after just 8 days wearing tongue tie and blinkers, with two wins at 5f on good but limited form at 6f (7th in one recent run) — the strong headgear combination and quick return suggest something is being aimed at, but the trip may stretch him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 17th of 20 on our figures, Vince L'Amour faces a stiff task, with his trainer striking at just 5% recently; a runner-up effort last time and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in practice who is shown in midfield purely because the rear is over-populated in this field — Gemma Tutty has two winners in 17 days and this horse has a 2nd and a 1st in recent outings, making it an interesting runner whose true style is closers' territory; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers the optimism slightly.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly mapped to midfield due to rear congestion — Philip Kirby trainer is cold (0/16 in 14 days), form reads 5-3-10-14-3 with the placings on good ground but zeros on turf recently; the displaced position and cold trainer angle make this speculative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has shown flashes, with a third last time out and a third four starts back keeping her honest; she has run over today's trip and going, and 128 lb from stall two is manageable, though a rating of 79 suggests she sits mid-pack on ability.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Oldest runner in the field at 10, a hold-up type mapped to midfield due to rear congestion and carrying pace headgear — three wins from five similar-going tries is a strong stat, Gemma Tutty is in form (2/17 in 14 days), and he has placed at this level repeatedly; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is the main caveat to what looks a lively each-way profile on pure stats.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mark's Choice faces a stiff ask from stall 17 carrying 125 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and shaped with some promise when third two starts back.

races.paceDynamic: Kats Bob is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, critically, faces no serious challenger for the lead — he should stride into a clear, comfortable advantage from the gates and dictate a steady, sustainable pace on good ground over six furlongs at Ripon. Behind him, a wall of prominent types — Woodstock, Magic Boy, Go Vince Go, Emperor Caradoc, Westmorian, Roach Power, Mythical Composer, and Who Wants Me — are all chasing the same early positions, guaranteeing a congested, scrimmaging battle for the flanks of Kats Bob in the first two furlongs that will create significant traffic and interference problems between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers. The hold-up brigade of Glory Hyde, Anaisa, Dorney Lake, Roberto Caro, and Vince L'Amour will be forced to sit even deeper than usual, needing a strong finishing gallop to burn through that traffic late. This race shape most favours horses that can secure a prominent pitch just behind the leader without getting caught in the early scramble — settled, economical front-of-field racers who travel cleanly and pounce between the two-furlong pole and the line. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Kats Bob will lead unchallenged, with Emperor Caradoc, Magic Boy, and Woodstock best placed to physically establish themselves in the next tier, while Mister Sox, Mythical Composer, and Roach Power are the most likely to be shuffled back from their natural pitch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kats Bob Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Kats Bob leads cleanly and a prominent racer stalks him efficiently without getting caught in the early scrimmage.
scenarios.body: Kats Bob sets a fair, uncontested pace and a well-positioned prominent horse tracks him into the straight before overhauling him inside the final furlong; the prominent runners who gain clean early berths travel sweetly and produce the best late kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Bunching Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the eight prominent types collide for position in the first two furlongs, creating a messy, uneven pace that suits a big finish from hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: The crowded early stages produce bumping, checking, and uneven fractions that slow the race sufficiently for the hold-up brigade to close with full momentum in the final two furlongs; horses with genuine late pace who find clear daylight through the traffic land this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Kats Bob Front-Runs and Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Kats Bob dictates a genuinely comfortable tempo and the prominent scrimmage behind him disorganises all chasers badly enough that no single rival travels cleanly.
scenarios.body: With every rival spending energy jostling for position or being blocked, Kats Bob's clean passage and well-judged early lead prove impossible to reel in; a steady gallop on good ground allows his front-running profile to bamboozle a chaotic field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If a fast early pace ignites through the prominent tussle and genuine hold-up horses get an unimpeded run up the stands rail or through the pack in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A strong, honest pace set by Kats Bob under pressure from the bunched prominent group burns the field out sufficiently for true closers to arrive with devastating late momentum; this shape is less likely given that several runners tagged as hold-up types are actually displaced prominent horses unlikely to be travelling as true hold-up runners.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion risk — with Woodstock, Magic Boy, Go Vince Go, Emperor Caradoc, Westmorian, Roach Power, Mythical Composer, and Who Wants Me all seeking early positions behind Kats Bob, expect significant bumping and checking between the 2f and 3f markers that could compromise multiple fancied runners.

Glory Hyde is the form horse of the race with three consecutive wins on good ground, but as a hold-up runner in a 20-runner field she will need a clear run through what promises to be a tightly packed pack — any traffic incident in the final two furlongs ends her chance immediately.

Kats Bob's front-running role is unchallenged in theory, but with 20 runners breaking behind him, any slow or awkward start from a wide draw could see him briefly crowded before he establishes his lead — William Pyle's handling of the opening furlong is worth watching closely.

Grant Wood (fades in finish) and Tolstoy (fades in finish, STYLE_FIT 0.90) are both flagged late-weakeners and are likely to be in the way of hold-up horses making their run in the final furlong — their positioning in the straight may create interference at the critical moment.

Dorney Lake returns after just 9 days on what looks a quick turnaround for Liam Bailey — he won his last start at standard going and has course-track place form; watch for market moves as a sign the yard is confident this is a live second-time-out follow-up

races.name: William Hill/MND Association Great St Wilfrid Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f performer on Good ground with two recent wins at this trip, and Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a useful weight-saving asset in a hot handicap; races prominently and is well-placed if he can hold a clean position in what will be a crowded prominent pack.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 15 on our figures, Lord Roxby faces a stiff ask against stronger company, and a speed rating of 84 gives him little chance on bare form, though he does arrive in decent nick — a winner last time out, 12 days ago — and has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: I'm Next
runners_data.note: Egan partner has been firing on 5f lately with back-to-back wins but now steps up to 6f — the extra furlong is unproven and the move to a longer trip under a 118lb burden is a genuine query against the pace shape here.
runners_data.comment: Beaten sixth last time out, he finds himself ranked 12th of 15 on our figures, and a trainer operating at just 5% over the past fortnight makes him hard to fancy, despite back-to-back wins three and four starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Musical Touch
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown he can win on Good ground at 6f and Fahey's yard is in fair form; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim reduces his weight nicely and his natural style of coming from off the pace suits a race likely to be run at a controlled early tempo.
runners_data.comment: Musical Touch won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, but an unplaced effort last time and a career-high 117 lb ask from stall nine give the handicapper's hold on him here.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent-racing type whose true style cannot be expressed here given how many front-runners are in this field — he has been struggling for form (three consecutive poor efforts) and the 51-day break adds uncertainty; the mismatch between style and race shape dampens confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and eight lengths back last time out, Eye Of Dubai arrives 51 days fresh but faces a stiff ask from stall one carrying 114 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 96 suggests ability worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Headgear-free runner who typically races up with the pace, but the field density means he is unlikely to find his natural berth; Tim Easterby's yard is active (4/73) and he has 6f Good form including a win, yet his chance hinges on finding a gap he may not get.
runners_data.comment: Beaten last time out after winning two starts back, Manila Scouse faces an uphill task ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, and the trainer's 5% strike rate over the past fortnight offers little encouragement; experience over today's trip and going is about the best that can be said.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Top-weighted at 138lbs, this Group-placed type drops into a 6f handicap off OR=109 but has failed to win in five runs and was well beaten last time at this trip on Good; the weight is crushing and despite the class pedigree his recent form offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Aramram showed smart form when second three starts back and back-to-back wins before that, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is a 56-day absence combined with a hefty 138 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Appleby's horse wants further than 6f based on his pattern of 7f wins and strong 7f form; his last three 6f starts have all produced poor performances and the trip shortfall on Good ground looks a fundamental concern regardless of his prominent style.
runners_data.comment: Royal Zabeel bounced back to win last time but was unplaced on his most recent start, so the form is a little in and out; he has experience of today's trip and going, and returns after a 35-day break carrying 133 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted for this run — the headgear combination is notable — but his recent form at 6f is a string of midfield finishes and he has not won since February; Jack Nicholls claims 3lbs but the horse needs to rediscover something.
runners_data.comment: Fast Track Harry arrives on the back of a solid second last time out, has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 103 suggests he holds strong claims off 124 lb — though his two unplaced runs before that comeback placed form may give some pause.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: Tudhope in the saddle is a strong plus at this track, and the visor remains in place following his recent win at 6f Good; he races prominently and has course-relevant form, making him one of the likelier horses to actually secure a forward pitch in the congested pack.
runners_data.comment: Dark Cloud Rising brings strong recent form to the table — a winner three starts back and placed in each of his last two starts — and has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that stall 15 gives him plenty to navigate early.

runners_data.name: Khafiz
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4yo drops back from 7-8f trips where he has been placed, and 6f looks potentially sharp — his hold-up style means he needs a genuine gallop to deliver his effort, and the controlled pace projected here is a mild concern despite the step down in trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Khafiz at least showed some improvement with back-to-back fourths in recent outings, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 120 lb from stall seven, the concern is whether he can find enough to break into the frame.

runners_data.name: Kodiac Thriller
runners_data.note: Has won at both 5f and 6f on Good ground and the visor stays on, suggesting the stable is trying to sharpen him; his natural front-running instinct is squeezed out by the race shape, and Cam Hardie will need to make a snap decision about whether to push for a position or drop in — neither is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Kodiac Thriller won last time out but ranks last of the 15 runners on our figures, and three unplaced efforts in his last six starts make him hard to fancy at the weights, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Fortification
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 3yo has useful 5f form and won here last time, but the field is stacked with prominent types meaning he is unlikely to find his natural forward position; the 49-day absence and youth (age 3 in a veteran-heavy field) add further layers of risk.
runners_data.comment: Fortification won four starts back but has been unplaced most recently, and 49 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 114 lb from stall 12, and his rating of 92 suggests some upside if sharper.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner — Walford's 8yo has won at 8f but the key here is his front-running role in a race no one will push him for; Andrew Mullen can dictate terms and set a tempo of his choosing, which is a significant tactical advantage in a 15-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 15 on our figures, It Just Takes Time is hard to fancy despite being lightly competitive in the weights at 114 lb; that ninth last time out overshadows a win two starts back, and experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Waugh's claim of 3lbs is useful on a 114lbs mark, and this Tim Easterby hold-up runner has won at 7f on Good — the 6f trip is the shortest he has run this season and whether he gets home may depend on how hard the race is run, but his clean-running style suits the projected late-stage chaos.
runners_data.comment: Brighton Boy has run over today's trip and going, and a win and a second feature in recent starts hint at ability, but three subsequent below-par efforts and a trainer firing at just 5% in the last fortnight give real cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Flight Control
runners_data.note: Unbeaten record on Good ground across all career runs (6/6) is striking and his form at 7f translates encouragingly to 6f; however, his naturally prominent style is squeezed out of its comfort zone in this field, and William Pyle is a relatively inexperienced rider in a tactical race that will demand quick decisions.
runners_data.comment: Flight Control won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid recent claims, though he carries 114 lb from stall 11 and our rating of 91 ranks him ninth of fifteen, suggesting he faces a stiff ask against the top end of this field.

races.paceDynamic: It Just Takes Time is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Andrew Mullen can control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop — this is not a race where the pace will be forced or manufactured artificially fast. The prominent cluster is severely overcrowded: Lord Roxby, I'm Next, Dark Cloud Rising, Aramram, Royal Zabeel, and Fast Track Harry all want to race close to the pace, creating inevitable traffic friction and jostling between the 2f and 3f pole. Fortification, Flight Control, Eye Of Dubai, Kodiac Thriller, and Manila Scouse are true prominent-racing types who have been displaced into a midfield mapping because there is simply no room for them all — the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position are Dark Cloud Rising (Tudhope, high-pressure draw experience), Lord Roxby (in-form, recent 6f winner) and I'm Next (sharp at the start historically). A controlled, single-paced gallop at the head of affairs with a congested prominent group favours hold-up horses who can sidestep the mid-race traffic and produce a sustained late challenge — Musical Touch, Khafiz, and Brighton Boy carry the profile most suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time bowls along uncontested and sets an honest but not frantic gallop that suits a steady-state sprint.
scenarios.body: Mullen dictates every yard, the prominent pack congests behind and burns energy fighting for position, leaving the front-runner with a crucial few lengths of daylight entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group burns itself out scrambling for position and the pace proves insufficient to sustain early leaders.
scenarios.body: Musical Touch and Khafiz track the chaos from off the pace, find clear running on the outside approaching the final furlong, and produce the strongest finishes in a race where front-runners tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to string out the field and one prominent type can break clear of the scrimmage two out.
scenarios.body: Dark Cloud Rising or Lord Roxby, both recent 6f winners at Good, manage to hold a clean position just behind the leader and quicken past It Just Takes Time inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion at the prominent end causes interference or significant checking two furlongs out, scrambling the race order entirely.
scenarios.body: A clean-travelling hold-up horse or a lightly-raced prominent type like Flight Control or Fortification threads through the gaps when rivals impede each other, benefiting from the disorder rather than causing it.

watchPoints.text: It Just Takes Time is the only horse with a clear lead, but if the prominent pack applies any early pressure — particularly from I'm Next or Lord Roxby — the pace could lift sharply and alter the entire race shape, so watch the first two furlongs closely.

The six prominent-type runners competing for roughly two or three positions at the head of the pack creates a high risk of interference and checking between 3f and 2f out — any horse caught in that squeeze loses all chance regardless of ability.

Aramram carries a crushing 138lbs at the top of the weights and has not won in five attempts — if he gets into a tussle for position early, he will set a fast early pace that benefits hold-up horses at the back, so his behaviour in the first furlong shapes the whole race.

Flight Control's 6/6 record on Good ground is a live angle, but William Pyle's inexperience in a 15-runner competitive handicap could cost ground in the scramble for position between the 3f and 2f poles — watch how cleanly he navigates the traffic.

Musical Touch and Brighton Boy both carry 3lb claiming riders and race from hold-up positions — if those riders time their runs correctly and find a gap on the outside entering the final 2f, the weight advantage over the heavier-burdened prominently-raced rivals could prove decisive.

races.name: William Hill World Free From MND Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Best Rate
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old who has won twice at a mile on Good ground recently — Joe Leavy is a booking worth noting and Richard Hannon's 4/55 strike rate is modest, but the horse's own form profile is strong for this trip and surface, operating naturally prominent.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after back-to-back wins, Best Rate arrives on a lively 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, and a rating of 96 suggests he holds strong claims from stall 1; the chief risk is that third last time out hints his form may be just dipping.

runners_data.name: Murashah
runners_data.note: Returning after 119 days off, which is the longest layoff flag in this field — Edward Bethell's yard sends them fit and the horse won on reappearance last time, but the freshness concern is real; natural prominent racer who has won twice over seven furlongs on Good and will be tested stepping to a mile.|
runners_data.comment: Murashah arrives on the back of two wins in his last five starts, including a victory latest, and has run over today's trip and going — with a trainer firing at 32% over the past fortnight, he looks a genuine threat; the one concern is a 119-day absence.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed in eleven of fifteen runs on Good going — Jason Watson takes over and the tongue-tie is retained; the horse's two second-place finishes at a mile on Good are directly relevant, though the zero-win record from fifteen Good-ground starts is a flag.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Andesite does bring distance and going experience to the table, alongside a speed rating that outstrips his official mark, yet fifth last time out and unplaced two starts back are harder to ignore for a gelding who needs to rediscover the consistency that brought back-to-back seconds earlier in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old arrives on just seven days' rest and has form figures of 0-9-0-6-1-6 recently — while fundamentally a prominent racer by preference, the congestion up front in this field means he is highly unlikely to secure that position and will be racing back further than he wants.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way out in the latest two of his last six starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Capital Guarantee is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters here, Andrew Mullen will press for the lead from the start — the recent form line includes a win over twelve furlongs on Soft but the sharp drop to a flat mile is a significant trip concern, and his 10-10-1-11-3 sequence over longer distances raises questions about whether he truly stays one mile at pace.|
runners_data.comment: High Point won three starts back but has been unplaced in both outings since, and with only a third to add in recent starts his form reads inconsistently; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 136 lb from stall six, and returns on a quick seven-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer for Michael Appleby and Harry Davies — without a win in six starts and without a win on Good going in two attempts, the OR=85 flatters a horse whose record shows consistency without a breakthrough; his best chance comes if the race develops into a truly run test over a mile.|
runners_data.comment: Jungle Ruler arrives on the back of consistent placing — second last time out and third two starts back — shaped by a top-ranked rating of 96, and he has run over today's trip before; the main concern is a yard operating at just five per cent in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: The most in-form runner in the field with three wins from his last six starts, all at a mile, all on Good or Firm — Ralph Beckett's colt wears a visor and is naturally prominent, and his 7/8 record on similar ground makes him an outstanding profile match for this surface, trip and going combination.|
runners_data.comment: Swiped arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, yet his speed rating of 71 gives the sharper types an edge, and carrying 134 lb from stall 2 adds further pressure on his claims.

runners_data.name: Advance Twentyfive
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Fahey yard who won over a mile on Good ground on his most recent start but has been inconsistent — the visor is retained, the 35-day layoff is within acceptable range, and Harry Russell keeps the ride; the drop back from ten furlongs to a mile should suit more than it hinders.|
runners_data.comment: Advance Twentyfive arrives on the back of a recent win and has experience of today's distance and going, giving him a solid each-way profile here. Carrying 132 lb from stall four, his last-five form is mixed but that latest success keeps him firmly in the picture.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old front-runner for Tim Easterby who will try to share the pace with High Point — David Allan has ridden him before and the horse has placed in seven of eleven recent Good-ground miles, but age and an OR of 71 mean leading for as long as possible is the only viable tactic.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Garden Oasis at least brings consistent placing form to the table — third last time out and a second two starts back — but a trainer strike-rate of just 5% over the past fortnight is a concern, and he faces ten rivals carrying 128 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this five-year-old for Tina Jackson (1/4 in 14 days, small sample) — a genuine prominent racer whose recent form is largely over ten and eleven furlongs, meaning the drop to a flat mile is a trip question; forced back into midfield by the field's pace congestion, he will not race where he wants.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, His Finest Hour is hard to fancy despite a bold recent record of placings; he has run over today's going before and comes here on a quick 12-day turnaround, but little else points his way.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist who has placed in all five of his most recent Good-ground starts over a mile — Sean Kirrane takes over from recent jockeys, the hood is fitted, and the zero-win record from ten similar runs at Ripon distances is the chief concern despite exceptional consistency.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of seconds and thirds that underlines his knack for finding one too good, Barley arrives here freshly enough on a seven-day turnaround but a cold trainer strike-rate and a ranking of tenth of eleven make him hard to fancy at the weights.

races.paceDynamic: High Point and Garden Oasis are the confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this flat Ripon mile, creating an honest, competitive gallop rather than an artificial crawl. With Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour both natural prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield due to traffic — meaning Best Rate, Murashah, Jungle Ruler and Swiped will be pressing hard just behind the leaders — the race is unlikely to be short of pace at any stage. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; High Point is most likely to actually lead, with Garden Oasis pressing alongside, while Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour will find themselves further back than ideal. A genuine, end-to-end gallop at Good ground on a flat track strongly favours horses with proven stamina for this mile trip who can travel powerfully in behind and finish with a sustained, rather than explosive, kick — making the hold-up runners and durable prominent types who settle well the most advantaged profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If High Point and Garden Oasis fight it out up front and empty inside the final two furlongs, freeing the track for finishers.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by the two leaders will stretch the field early and set up a true test of stamina over the mile, allowing horses who settle in mid-to-rear to unleash sustained finishes. Andesite, Barley and Advance Twentyfive — all proven hold-up operators on Good ground over this trip — are ideally positioned to exploit the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is competitive but not blistering and a horse tracking just off the leaders sustains their momentum into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Best Rate and Swiped both have the profile to sit comfortably just off the pace in second or third, maintain their rhythm through the home straight and prove too strong for the closers. Swiped's recent hat-trick of wins over a mile on Good ground makes this shape particularly compelling for that runner, while Best Rate's back-to-back wins at the trip are equally relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Last Long
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more measured than expected and one of the leaders — most likely High Point — controls proceedings without burning too much energy.
scenarios.body: High Point's record over shorter trips suggests he may not truly stay a flat mile under pressure, but if Garden Oasis fails to push the tempo and the field settles, an uncontested lead could allow a surprise front-running display. Garden Oasis at 11 years old has the consistency on Good ground to factor if gifted an easy time, but age and OR=71 limit the ceiling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Hold-Ups Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is chaotic enough to cause interference or bunching mid-race, allowing the deepest closers to scythe through late.
scenarios.body: This shape requires Barley and Advance Twentyfive to find clear daylight very late and is contingent on a messy race developing — less likely given experienced riders and a straightforward flat track. Barley's remarkable consistency (all recent runs placed on Good ground over this exact trip) means it would benefit most if this chaos scenario materialised.

watchPoints.text: High Point and Garden Oasis — watch whether either blinks in the duel for the lead early; if one of them goes hard and the other matches, the resulting burn-up will be significant enough to shape the entire race in favour of closers.

Capital Guarantee and His Finest Hour — both natural prominent types forced wide of their comfort zone by field congestion; if either expends energy fighting for position in the first two furlongs they are effectively out of the race before halfway.

Murashah — 119 days off is the most significant freshness flag in the race; watch in the betting market for any late support that suggests stable confidence, as a fit-at-home angle could make that layoff irrelevant.

Swiped — the visor is retained and the Good-ground mile record is outstanding; if he settles smoothly just off the pace rather than getting involved in the early scrap, his profile is the single strongest fit for however this race is run.

Barley — consistent to a fault over this exact trip and going, Sean Kirrane's instructions will be to come from the back; watch where he is at the two-furlong marker — if daylight appears late, his stamina profile makes him dangerous in a scenario where the front-runners have emptied.

races.name: Ashley Smith Memorial William Hill Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is a hold-up filly who finished sixth twice over 10f on Soft before a seventh on the same surface — three runs in similar conditions without a win or place, and now stepping up to 1m4f for the first time; Rhys Clutterbuck takes over and the trip extension is the main unknown, though the Good ground is no concern.
runners_data.comment: Musical Accord has experience of today's going and carries a workable 135 lb, but she arrives winless in her last three starts and a 72-day absence is the key risk to her fitness sharpness.

runners_data.name: Talitha Rouge
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's filly has a solid placed record in Good-ground handicaps at 10-12f — two third places and a fourth from four runs on comparable ground — making her the most consistent performer in the field against her style; Tudhope is a significant booking and her 23-day return to form is reassuring, though she will need to be produced from the rear against a front-runner who will control the tempo.
runners_data.comment: Talitha Rouge shaped with promise when third two starts back and third again four starts back, and our rating of 74 sees her share top billing; yet to score in her last four starts, and her recent sixth is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old is the race's only front-runner and has strong recent form to justify it — a win at 11f on Good followed by a runner-up at 12f on Good; with no challenger for the lead and Oisin Orr aboard, he faces a straightforward opportunity to dictate from flag to finish, and his Going record at the trip is directly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Runners-up last time out and a winner two starts back, Clocker arrives in fine shape just 17 days after that placed effort, with her trainer firing at 32% over the past fortnight. She has experience of today's trip and going, and her 130 lb burden is the one factor to monitor.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Standard but has struggled on turf — six runs, no further wins — and her true running style is hold-up, though the crowded rear means she is effectively mapped to midfield in this race shape; Jason Watson will need to position her more aggressively than is natural, and a STYLE_FIT discount applies as she is unlikely to get her preferred pitch.
runners_data.comment: Blue Tulip won last time out to arrive here in form, but three finishes of sixth, sixth and fifth in her last five starts underline the inconsistency, and she ranks last on our figures among these five runners, making her genuinely hard to fancy despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Skirt Around
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's runner is absent for 72 days, his trainer has no winners from 16 runners in the last 14 days, and her form string of 643-87 shows regression; her natural hold-up style is also displaced by the congested rear group, placing her out of role in a race already set up to suit Clocker — the combination of layoff, trainer form, and positional difficulty makes her profile hard to endorse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Skirt Around does hold going experience and her rating of 69 suggests she is better than her official mark implies, with a third three starts back hinting at residual ability — though a 72-day absence is the obvious question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Clocker is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, Oisin Orr can dictate terms at a pace entirely of his own choosing over 1m4f on Good ground at Ripon. With Clocker able to control tempo from the front, the race is likely to be run at a measured, sustainable gallop — potentially a moderately-run affair that compresses the field and reduces the advantage of coming from off the pace. Musical Accord, Talitha Rouge, Blue Tulip, and Skirt Around are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the rear of the field will be congested and late closers face an uncertain run. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Blue Tulip and Skirt Around, both true rear-runners, have been redistributed to midfield positions they are unlikely to command organically. This race shape strongly favours Clocker and any runner capable of tracking the leader prominently, as a soft pace set from the front will likely reward the horse who gets closest to the action early and has the class to quicken from a handy position in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clocker Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker bowls along in front at a comfortable gallop and none of the hold-up types can mount a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Clocker sets a measured pace that suits his recent form — a win at 11f on Good and a runner-up at 12f on Good — and the lack of pressure allows him to conserve energy before kicking clear in the Ripon straight; the hold-up heavy field will be closing into a slowing pace rather than a true-run gallop, blunting their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker's steady pace eventually compresses the field enough that a well-placed hold-up runner picks up the scraps late.
scenarios.body: Talitha Rouge's consistent placed form in similar Good-ground races at 10-12f gives her the profile to pick up late if gaps open in the straight, particularly with Daniel Tudhope's tactical intelligence aboard; Musical Accord is also a possibility if the pace is genuinely slow and she can get a clear run from the rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed runners manages to travel close enough to Clocker's pace that they can mount a race-fit challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Blue Tulip, racing somewhat out of natural role having been mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, would need to secure a tracking berth early — a significant ask given her form profile; if she does, her Flat-course stamina at 12f over good-adjacent ground could prove competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Clocker slows the tempo to a crawl and the race becomes a sprint finish from two furlongs out, scrambling the form book.
scenarios.body: A truly muddling pace would turn the outcome into a lottery across all five runners, but Skirt Around's genuine hold-up style — redistributed to midfield — means she is poorly placed to exploit the shape even in this scenario, and her 72-day absence adds further risk; this scenario's outcome would be difficult to call but structurally benefits any runner with tactical speed.

watchPoints.text: Clocker's ability to get a clean, uncontested lead is the race's pivotal factor — watch the first furlong to see whether any runner attempts to match his early pace, as even brief pressure could change the entire tempo calculus.

Talitha Rouge's positioning in the early stages is key — if Tudhope can situate her second or third early rather than trailing in the rear, her Good-ground placed form makes her the most credible threat to Clocker in the straight.

Blue Tulip and Skirt Around are both true hold-up horses racing in a field where the rear is overcrowded; watch whether either can secure a midfield berth at the start, as failure to do so will leave them with too much ground to make up on a front-runner setting a comfortable pace.

The 1m4f trip at Ripon is a stamina test for a field of three-year-old fillies, most of whom have limited experience at this distance — watch whether Clocker's Good-ground form at 11-12f translates, or whether the extra yardage exposes any fitness concerns after a 17-day turnaround.

races.name: Harrogate Comedy Festival Coming This Autumn Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Tim Easterby who handles good ground well (13 qualifying runs, one win five places), but at 6 years old and with only 3 days since last run, freshness is fine; genuine rear-of-field type who will need a gap to open in a very congested field.
runners_data.comment: Sunny Orange shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and third three starts back, and has run over today's distance and going before, making him a genuine contender from stall five at 140 lb; the main concern is a reappearance just three days after his last run, with the yard in a lean spell.

runners_data.name: War And Love
runners_data.note: Drops back in trip from 7f-8f sprints to 1m2f, which is a significant query, and has zero wins from 8 qualifying good-ground starts; a hold-up horse by nature who has struggled even at shorter, making this extra distance a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but the consistency of a third last time out and a third four starts back gives War And Love a chance of mixing it with the principals; she has run over today's going before, though 140 lb from stall nine is no light burden.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner, rated 59, who has won over this exact 10f trip on good ground and is drawn to dictate; STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) noted as it is technically listed as prominent, but its role as pace-setter here is clear — everything hinges on whether it can control the tempo from the front.
runners_data.comment: Winner three starts back and third two starts back, Kitsune Power arrives on a quick turnaround carrying 139 lb from stall four, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; a sluggish trainer strike-rate is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Woodleigh
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's five-year-old has won over 10f on good and is capable, but is a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot on the map due to overcrowding at the rear; its best form (2 wins) has come on softer ground and this good surface is a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Woodleigh has winning form in his last six starts, scoring back-to-back victories four and five starts back, and returns here on a good freshness of 17 days with experience of today's trip and going; the concern is that his three most recent efforts have all been out of the frame.

runners_data.name: Marlena's Prince
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old for Micky Hammond with only four career runs, making assessment difficult; going is flagged UNKNOWN, 62-day absence adds uncertainty, but hold-up style and step up in trip could suit if there is something here we haven't seen yet.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Inconsistent record — wins at 8f but repeatedly beaten out of sight at 10f — and although trainer Christopher Kellett has a rare strike in recent form, this horse is a true hold-up type pushed to midfield; form string of 783818 reflects the boom-or-bust nature.
runners_data.comment: Daring Leader showed he can find the winner's enclosure when scoring two starts back, but eighths on either side of that win and again last time out are hard to ignore; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 136 lb from stall six presents a stiff enough ask for a horse rated just 56.

runners_data.name: Magic Runner
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old has only one qualifying run on good going from 15 starts, which is a significant surface concern despite the going being officially Good; a hold-up horse by inclination squeezed into midfield on the map, with poor recent form (355705) doing nothing to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Magic Runner at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and her rating of 62 edges above the official mark of 56; the weight of 136 lb from stall three may, however, test her further.

runners_data.name: Casilli
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran returning after 366 days off, a serious red flag regardless of style or going; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field congestion, and the combination of age, lengthy absence, and consistent midfield finishes on good ground makes this very hard to support.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and carrying 134 lb from stall two, Casilli has experience of today's trip and conditions, but she is winless in her last five starts and returns from a 366-day absence, which is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 8f on good and standard, winning zero from seven qualifying starts but placing twice; this nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse compressed into a midfield slot — the natural style is at the rear, not where the map shows, and the shorter trip relative to some recent runs is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts despite three runner-up finishes, Little Ted steps back up having run over today's trip and going before, but a struggling yard at 5% over the past fortnight is a concern, and his latest sixth leaves him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Feliz Navidad
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old from David O'Meara's powerful yard, with Daniel Tudhope — a top jockey — taking the ride, which is an obvious positive angle; only three career runs limit the form assessment, but all three on good ground and O'Meara's 9/54 T14 figure shows stable in decent nick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Feliz Navidad faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort, but the 132 lb burden makes improvement hard to foresee.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Two wins from her last six including back-to-back 8f good-ground victories, and only 2 days since last run suggests excellent freshness; the step up to 10f is the one question mark, but the form is strong, the going suits perfectly, and Daragh Bourke's yard is running at 2/5 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Saxon Grace arrives in fine nick with back-to-back wins, but a two-day turnaround is a stern test of her recovery, and 137 lb from stall 11 adds further to her burden despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Horwich
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's three-year-old has no wins and no places from 12 qualifying good-ground starts — a damning statistic — and despite being a hold-up type shown in midfield due to redistribution, recent form (046606) is deeply uninspiring at sprint trips let alone this 10f test.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Horwich at least has experience over today's trip and arrives here 25 days fresh, though a weight of 130 lb from stall 15 and a string of sixths and unplaced efforts make a turnaround hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Hijo de La Luna
runners_data.note: Versatile stayer who has run over trips ranging from 11f to 16f and handles good ground (7 qualifying runs), but stepping back down to 10f from those longer distances is unconventional; wears a visor, and the trainer's T14 of 0/2 is not encouraging — a true hold-up type in a congested rear.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures and rated just 47 officially, Hijo de La Luna is hard to fancy despite a third last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, but five unimpressive efforts either side of a sole recent win make him difficult to support from stall 8 at 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Riddikulus
runners_data.note: Interesting profile — two wins over 10f and 12f on good ground with a blinkers flag, and recent form (444141) shows genuine ability at this type of trip; Grant Tuer's yard is live at 1/5 over 14 days, and this is one of the more credible hold-up horses in the field despite the redistribution note.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our assessments and rated a mere 53, Riddikulus faces a stiff task, and four fourths in her last six starts underline the inconsistency, though she does boast two wins in that spell, has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a fresh 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Tiberio Force
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Simon Whitaker who has been placed once from 9 qualifying starts on good or standard, and six consecutive finishing positions of 6th or worse paint a clear picture; wears blinkers and is a hold-up type shuffled to midfield on the pace map — hard to make a case here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than sixth throughout that sequence, Tiberio Force is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; the 15-day turnaround at least suggests freshness.

races.paceDynamic: Kitsune Power is the sole confirmed front runner in this 15-runner 1m2f handicap at Ripon and, facing no meaningful pressure from another genuine pace-setter, is positioned to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop on good turf. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Woodleigh, Horwich, Magic Runner, Daring Leader, Casilli, Little Ted, Hijo de La Luna, Riddikulus, Hijo de La Luna, and Tiberio Force are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield slots on the pace map simply because there is no room for them all at the rear in a race this shape. Sunny Orange, War And Love, Feliz Navidad, and Saxon Grace will also be seeking cover, meaning the rear and midfield will be congested and runners will inevitably jostle for position throughout. With Kitsune Power able to dictate an uncontested, measured tempo from the front, this race shape strongly favours the prominent or pace-positive profile — horses travelling in the slipstream of a lone, unhurried front runner who can track, conserve energy, and pounce in the straight without the traffic problems that will afflict the overcrowded hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kitsune Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kitsune Power secures the lead uncontested and sets a measured, sustainable gallop throughout the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Kitsune Power controls from the front, takes the field into the straight at a rhythm entirely of her own choosing, and a horse sitting second or third can simply follow the leader and peel off into a winning challenge; the hold-up horses face a wall of traffic and are unable to quicken through.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off Kitsune Power's pace tracks smoothly and produces the decisive move turning for home.
scenarios.body: The race is run at a controlled tempo that suits a horse settled two to four lengths off the leader, who sweeps past in the final two furlongs without requiring a devastating sprint; the true hold-up horses are boxed in or simply too far back to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to string the field out and create gaps for late-finishing hold-up types.
scenarios.body: A horse held up with cover finds a clear run from two furlongs out and finishes strongly through tiring rivals, but this scenario is undermined by the fact that most of the so-called hold-up horses in this field are redistributed types unlikely to hold a true rearward position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Kitsune Power is pressured unexpectedly or the field bunches into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A muddling, slowly-run race with no true pacesetter breaks into a sprint that can theoretically suit any positional type, but with this many runners and a congested midfield the most organised prominent horse holds a marginal edge; form counts for little in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Kitsune Power (Amie Waugh, 3lb claim) sets the entire pace shape — if anything causes it to be pressured or headed early (e.g. a rival breaking smartly), the race dynamic collapses and hold-up horses become more dangerous than this analysis suggests.

Saxon Grace ran just 2 days ago and steps up markedly in trip to 1m2f for the first time — watch the betting to gauge stable confidence, as the freshness angle and good-ground form are compelling but the distance query is real.

The congested hold-up cluster of Riddikulus, Sunny Orange, Daring Leader, and Magic Runner will all be jostling for the same limited racing room on the straight — a split-second gap or a seamless passage will separate the placers from the also-rans among these types.

Casilli (Billy Garritty, Michael & David Easterby) returns from 366 days off — watch whether it is heavily backed despite the layoff, which would suggest the stable knows the horse is ready; otherwise treat with significant caution.

Feliz Navidad carries Daniel Tudhope, one of the top riders in the north — any market move for this lightly-raced O'Meara three-year-old over an unexplored trip should be noted as an informational signal rather than ignored.
